verdict.rationale: FFmpeg documents chaining processing stages inside a single invocation. A filtergraph can deinterlace then resize, the transcoding pipeline runs demux, decode, filter, encode and mux together, and the product can stream output. That partly covers convert-then-optimize as one job. There is no first-party job definition, multi-step orchestration, or watched-folder workflow; users write their own batch wrappers, and that workaround earns no credit. Missing for 10: watched-folder or trigger-based workflows, a named multi-step job/workflow definition that includes a delivery step, and hands-on evidence of end-to-end chained convert-optimize-deliver jobs.

support.subject: As an ops lead, I can chain steps (convert, then optimize, then deliver) into one job or watched workflow

citations.quote: A simple video filtergraph that performs deinterlacing (using the yadif deinterlacer) followed by resizing (using the scale filter)
all the major components of the transcoding pipeline (demuxers, decoders, filters, encodes, muxers) now run in parallel.
A complete, cross-platform solution to record, convert and stream audio and video.
